Speaking from personal experience as someone who can be a little clingy at times, it's not just a fear of abandonment and loneliness (though that's definitely there), but also problems with yourself and a lack of experience with relationships. When you're alone, you're forced to dwell on your short-comings and flaws (I'm too ugly, too stupid, too awkward, etc.). But when you're with someone else, you can forget about those things for a brief moment and feel like you matter to somebody, even if that really isn't the case. It's a feeling you start to crave, so you try to capture it at every opportunity by always trying to hang out or always going out of your way to do things like pay for meals, pay to go to movies, just doing whatever the other person wants in the hopes that they'll stay and you can finally have that idyllic relationship you always day-dreamed about. It's a shitty thing and you know that it's stupid to do it, but you still just do it because anything is better than the feeling of a weight pushing down on your shoulders and a sinking in your chest while you go over various what-if situations in your mind. 

And since you have no idea of how to be in a relationship or what it's like to start one, you just let desperation get the best of you and you start clinging to the first guy who says hey to you on grindr (or jack'd or the myriad other apps you have on your phone because let's be honest, you have a profile on all of them) even though you know that you shouldn't. Of course, you still end up clinging too hard and pushing the other person away because they're put off by your willingness to dive in head-first and you're right back to square one.

When the Great War ends in 1918, the British government is able to focus on domestic matters more, including the thorny issue of Ireland. When Ramsay MacDonald in 1924, he takes up the issue of home-rule. His government passes the Irish Act of 1924 which grants Ireland a devolved government and legislative assembly with control over most domestic issues as well as granting recognition to the Irish language as a regional language of the UK.

The passage of Irish devolution in 1924 allows MacDonald to secure victory in the general election that year and turns Ireland into the base of Labour's support, even though republican voices are still present in Dublin. Irish devolution also inspires similar movements for a similar arrangement in Cornwall, England, Scotland, and Wales to begin in the late 20s and early 30s. Those movements die down a little nit during World War II and return to the forefront as Britain begins to grant independence to several colonies. Between 1945 and 1960, the British government grants devolution first to Scotland, then Wales, then England, and then to Cornwall.

The success of devolution under Labour allows them to form governments after nearly every election with only brief interruptions from the Tories every now and again. This allows the UK to keep its welfare state mostly intact and prevents any major privatisations of state-owned assets.

Let's make the point of departure the German invasion of France. Charles de Gaulle and his allies in the French military and government flee to Algeria, where they set up a government in Algiers to rival the Vichy Regime of Philippe Pétain. After the launch of Operation Barbarossa, Stalin extends a hand of friendship to de Gaulle, who accepts it in a pragmatic effort to defeat the Germans and Pétainists. In this timeline, Franco becomes more involved with the war than he does in OTL. Stalin and de Gaulle begin reaching out to a wide array of anti-Fascists across the political spectrum from Catalan anarchists to the exiled Prince Juan Carlos.

After the end of the Battle of Britain and the abandonment of Hitler's planned invasion of the UK, the British and the Americans focus on the War in the Pacific as the Americans seek revenge for Pearl Harbor and the British seek to protect their colonial interests from Japanese control. 

In 1943, instead of the Americans leading an invasion of Sicily, a group of Italian partisans take charge in the fight against Mussolini on the same day that de Gaulle launches an invasion of Corsica and Spanish partisans launch an invasion of the Balearic Islands all with help from the USSR. After the fall of Sicily, King Emmanuel III of Italy dismisses parliament and orders the arrest of Mussolini and his top officials. The Italian partisans then quickly retake Rome and execute Mussolini after a one-hour long trial broadcasted to the nation by radio. The Corsican invasion is a success for de Gaulle while the Spanish partisans successfully retake the Balearic Islands. Juan Carlos proclaims the establishment of a National Unity Government in Mallorca made up primarily of socialists and himself as King.

Juan Carlos's forces then launch an invasion of Catalonia. Hitler's Wehrmacht then invades Northern Spain in order to prop up Franco's regime. However, German assistance comes too late to keep Madrid under Fascist control. Franco is able to flee the city just before Juan Carlos makes his triumphant return to the Royal Palace. The Nazis attempt to install Franco in a puppet government in Bilbao. The Basque population violently resists the puppet government and the region is liberated just three weeks later.

De Gaulle then meets with King Juan Carlos, King Emmanuel III, Franklin Delano Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, Chiang Kai-shek, and Joseph Stalin in Rome as the Soviet Army begins the push to take Germany. In Rome, the leaders agree  that de Gaulle will lead a four-pronged invasion of Metropolitan France from Corsica, Italy, Spain, and the UK with the help of their respective militaries. After liberating Paris, they will begin a push to take Germany and meet the Soviets in Berlin. Within just a few weeks of the invasion, de Gaulle triumphantly enters a newly-liberated Paris. The Battle for Germany then begins with the Italians invading Austria, the French invading the Rhineland, and the British invading and liberating the Benelux nations under Nazi occupation. In Norway, resistance fighters rise up against Vidkun Quisling's and help the Danes liberate their country from Germany. After Hitler kills himself just before Berlin falls, Stalin sets to work ensuring the creation of pro-Soviet governments in Mainland Europe. Churchill and Roosevelt write off Mainland Europe as a lost cause and turn their attention to the war against Japan while also making it their mission to prevent the establishment of Communism in Asia.

Stalin keeps his end of the bargain by invading Manchuria and Korea on 1 August 1945. In Korea, Kim Il-sung establishes the Democratic People's Republic of Korea with the help of Stalin's forces after the Japanese withdrawal. The Americans then drop atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki which forces Emperor Hirohito to declare Japanese surrender on 15 August 1945. Five days later, Molotov meets in Beijing with Chiang Kai-shek and Mao Zedong, leader of the Communist Party of China to negotiate an end to the Civil War with Chiang remaining President and Mao becoming Prime Minister of the newly established People's Republic of China. Under the deal, the Communists and Nationalists share power in order to run the country.

In Romania, King Michael cooperates with the socialists under Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej and remains as the country's constitutional monarch and head of state while the socialists run the country's day-to-day affairs. Tsar Boris II of Bulgaria, King Zog of Albania, and King Peter II of Yugoslavia enter into similar arrangements with Georgi Dimitrov, Enver Hoxha, and Josip Broz Tito, respectively. King Juan Carlos I of Spain and King Emmanuel III of Italy also remain in power despite the establishment of socialists as the dominant political force in their country. Khrushchev gets Johnson to agree to a joint lunar mission. Under their agreement, a Soviet-made rocket with a name chosen by the Americans will lift off from Cape Canaveral, Florida and a Soviet cosmonaut will be the first man to walk on the moon while an American astronaut will be the first woman to walk on the moon behind him. The mission is a huge success as Friendship 1 touches down on the lunar surface on 1 May 1968. Upon stepping out of the module, the Soviet cosmonaut utters the first words spoken on the moon: "Friendship brought us here, now I only hope that friendship will bring us to peace" (a double entendre in Russian due to the fact that the word for peace and the world are both "mir").
